What it looks like: Not sure where to stand yet: back or net, left or right.
Statements (I can...): I know the basic spots: both back, or both at the net.

Spanish: Posición de espera y split step
Definition: Knees bent, racket up, and a small hop as the opponent hits.
When to use it: Before every shot you receive.
What it looks like: Knows the ready position and uses it on slow balls, but is often late on fast ones.
Statements (I can...):
I stand in a ready position between shots.
I'm ready before slow balls arrive.
Warning questions: Do fast balls catch you flat-footed?

Spanish: Posición de espera y split step
Definition: Knees bent, racket up, and a small hop as the opponent hits.
When to use it: Before every shot you receive.
What it looks like: Usually ready before the opponent hits. Split step is inconsistent.
Statements (I can...):
I'm ready before the opponent hits.
I do a small split step as they hit.
Warning questions: Are you still moving when the opponent hits?

Definition: Moving up to the net together and staying there.
When to use it: After a good lob, chiquita or return.
What it looks like: Nothing consistent yet. Sometimes ends up at the net at the wrong time, or stays at the net all the time. Volleys are often a block that goes into the net or too high.
Statements (I can...): I sometimes play at the net.
Warning questions: Do you end up at the net at the wrong time, or stay there when you're in trouble?

I take the net when the chance is clear.
Once I'm there, I stay with steady volleys.

Warning questions: Do you lose the net after one lob?
